description: Kintsugi adapts the developmental-psychology mechanism of joint attention to byte-size local models so that multi-agent systems can hold a shared goal. A deterministic protocol holds the commitment record (focus holder, phase, contention); small adapted models serve as the perceptual layer, maintaining a compressed goal-state and producing canonical uptake restatements that are verified against the record. Divergence is surfaced as a first-class repair event in the shared log — the gold seams — rather than hidden. Authority never transfers to the models. This deposit contains the full manuscript source, its bibliography, and the build tooling for the submission PDF.
title: Kintsugi: Joint Attention for Byte-Size Models — Shared Goals in Multi-Agent Systems Through Verified Uptake and Visible Repair
